nodes.text: Let\[ f(\theta) = \sum_{0\leq k\leq n}c_k e^{ik\theta}\]be a trigonometric polynomial all of whose roots are real, such that $\max_{\theta\in [0,2\pi]}\lvert f(\theta)\rvert=1$. Then\[\int_0^{2\pi}\lvert f(\theta)\rvert \mathrm{d}\theta \leq 4.\]

#225 : [Er40b,p.957] [Er57] [Er61,p.248] [Ha74] analysis This is Problem 4.20 in [Ha74] , where it is attributed to Erdős. This was solved independently by Kristiansen [Kr74] (only in the case when $c_k\in\mathbb{R}$) and Saff and Sheil-Small [SaSh74] (for general $c_k\in \mathbb{C}$). (The original proof of Kristiansen contained an error which was later fixed in [Kr76] .)
